purpose: Reviewed defensive seed cases for authority/evidence reasoning. These are evaluation seeds, not offensive playbooks.

scenario.claim: The agent can only call one read-only tool.
observed: UI shows a single tool permission.
Wallet module exposes an admin-upgrade role controlled by a separate signer.
The current module implementation can be replaced without the agent key changing.

expected_reasoning: Separate advertised agent permission from effective module-admin authority.
Identify the admin signer as a higher authority path.
Do not conclude least privilege from the UI permission alone.
cases.expected_conclusion: Permission scope is not fully trustworthy until upgrade/admin authority is included in the authority graph.

scenario.claim: A valid signature authorizes exactly one payment.
observed: Signature verifies.
Nonce is present.
No evidence shows the signed domain contains chain identifier or destination contract.
The same account format exists on two chains.

expected_reasoning: A valid signature proves signer possession but not one-chain-only intent.
Nonce scope cannot be assumed to be global across chains.
Missing domain evidence requires confidence reduction or abstention.
cases.expected_conclusion: Single-payment authorization cannot be established from the supplied evidence.

scenario.claim: Recovery completed, so the compromised key is no longer dangerous.
observed: Owner key was rotated.
A prior session key remains listed as valid until a future timestamp.
Recovery documentation does not show session-key revocation.

expected_reasoning: Recovery and delegated-session revocation are distinct controls.
Old owner compromise does not prove residual delegated authority is removed.
Post-recovery authority inventory is required.
cases.expected_conclusion: Recovery is incomplete from a security-authority perspective while residual delegated keys remain valid.

scenario.claim: The proof verified, therefore the reported reserve condition is correct.
observed: Proof verification returns true.
Public inputs are available.
No reviewed mapping is supplied between the business claim and the circuit statement.
Verifier version is known.

expected_reasoning: Verification establishes consistency with a statement, not correctness of the external business interpretation.
Require statement-to-claim binding before accepting the reserve conclusion.
cases.expected_conclusion: Cryptographic validity alone is insufficient to establish the claimed reserve condition.

scenario.claim: The transfer is final because a preconfirmation was issued.
observed: Sequencer preconfirmation exists.
Transaction is visible in the L2 execution view.
L1 settlement has not reached the required finality condition.

expected_reasoning: Separate preconfirmation, execution visibility, settlement, and finality.
Do not collapse latency guarantees into settlement guarantees.
cases.expected_conclusion: The transfer may be preconfirmed/executed but is not yet proven final under the supplied settlement state.

scenario.claim: The intent succeeded because the solver marked the order complete.
observed: Solver status is complete.
Destination transaction exists.
Expected recipient balance change is absent from the observed post-state.
Payment finality to the solver is unknown.

expected_reasoning: Solver status is not authoritative evidence of requested user outcome.
Actual post-state must be compared to intent semantics.
Execution success and solver payment finality are separate.
cases.expected_conclusion: The requested outcome is not established and appears inconsistent with the observed destination state.
expected_remediation: verify intent hash and resolver mapping

scenario.claim: The agent is trusted because it has 500 positive reputation entries.
observed: Positive entries exist.
No evidence establishes independent rater diversity.
No validator-method evidence is provided.
The agent requests a payment permission larger than its task scope requires.

expected_reasoning: Treat reputation as corroborating signal, not authority.
Check rater provenance and validation method.
Evaluate payment permission independently using least privilege.
cases.expected_conclusion: The reputation count does not justify the requested payment authority.

scenario.claim: The runtime is trusted because a TEE attestation passed yesterday.
observed: Attestation signature is valid.
Measurement matched the approved image at issuance time.
Current runtime version and current TCB status are unavailable.
Key-release policy is not supplied.

expected_reasoning: A previously valid attestation does not establish current runtime state.
Freshness, runtime drift, TCB state, and key-release policy are independent evidence requirements.
cases.expected_conclusion: Current trusted-runtime status cannot be established from the available evidence.
